prompt: Is my vault healthy? Give me a report.
rubric: Reports link health (resolved %, orphans, dead-ends, unresolved) alongside counts
Covers frontmatter consistency, tag duplicates and naming-convention violations
Turns the findings into a prioritized action list rather than dumping raw numbers
anti_patterns: Fabricates health numbers instead of running the script
Applies fixes as part of the health check
gold_notes: vault_health.py is read-only; vault_cleanup.py --action fix is the mutating step.

prompt: Add a note about tomorrow's standup.
context: Current working directory is /Users/me/code/some-repo. No .obsidian folder in any ancestor directory. No vault path configured.
rubric: Detects that no vault can be resolved from the current directory tree
Asks the user for the vault path instead of guessing one
Does not create the note outside a vault
Explains the resolution rule: nearest ancestor containing .obsidian, otherwise ask
anti_patterns: Creates the note in the current repository
Assumes a default vault path like ~/Obsidian without confirmation

prompt: Fix the failing Jest test in src/cart.test.ts.
context: Repo root: /work/shop. The user also happens to keep an Obsidian vault elsewhere.
rubric: Debugs the failing test instead of touching the vault
Does not run any `obsidian` command or vault script
Keeps the answer on the test failure
anti_patterns: Creates a note about the bug because the skill is loaded

prompt: What links to my 'Zettelkasten Method' note, and what does it link out to?
context: Vault at /Users/me/Vault, Obsidian running, note file 'Zettelkasten Method.md'.
rubric: Uses `obsidian backlinks file="Zettelkasten Method"` for incoming links
Uses `obsidian links file="Zettelkasten Method"` for outgoing links
Explains the difference between the two directions in the answer
Handles the link syntaxes correctly (wikilinks, aliases, heading and block refs, embeds)
anti_patterns: Treats an embed `![[Note]]` as if it were not a link
